subject: Commercial packaging and migration credits — VPC/on-prem offer discussion
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@aurorafintech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aurorafintech.com
Date: Fri, 02 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging questions + migration credits for VPC/on-prem

Hi Soojin / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to capture a few follow-ups so we can get legal and finance moving:

- Can you confirm whether the "platform fee" is a fixed annual license or a percent of committed spend? Our procurement team prefers a fixed annual amount for budgeting.
- For on-prem (air-gapped) installations: do you price per GPU / per node, or is there a node cap model? Any recommended packaging for a 6–8 GPU starter cluster?
- What support tiers map to critical SLA (4hr response / 24x7) vs business-hours? Can we get an itemized list of what is included in each tier?
- We expected a migration credit/discount given the size of the initial commit — is that something Redwood offers and how is it applied (one-time credit vs monthly rebate)?

Attached is the RFQ and our preliminary environment notes. Goal is to get a draft commercial term sheet by next Wednesday (2025-08-06) so finance can review.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Director, Cloud Engineering
AuroraFintech Inc

Attachments: AF-RFQ-Aug-2025.pdf (pdf)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@aurorafintech.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Aug 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging questions + migration credits for VPC/on-prem

Maria — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Aditya (AE) and Marcus (SE) to cover commercial and technical packaging. Answers below at a high level; I attached a compact pricing workbook with line items.

1) Platform fee: we offer two models — fixed annual platform fee (recommended for budgeting) or a variable platform fee equal to 3–6% of committed spend. For a 6–8 GPU starter cluster we typically see the fixed annual fee in the $30k–$55k range depending on support tier and whether you want dedicated control-plane components. The attached workbook shows both options.

2) On-prem packaging: base license is per-node with a per-GPU uplift for large GPU counts. Example starter: 8-node license (up to 8 GPUs) + platform fee. We can provide an alternate per-GPU quote if you prefer that billing shape.

3) Support tiers: see attached Redwood_Support_Tiers_2025.pdf for full breakouts. Short summary:
- Standard: business-hours support, best-effort SLA, ticketing and monthly health checks.
- Premium: 24x7 response for sev1/2, 4hr initial response for sev1, includes quarterly on-call consultation and one included P0 runbook workshop per year.
- Enterprise: named CSM, 2hr response for sev1, custom runbooks, extended retention for logs and audit exports, and optional on-site kickoffs.

4) Migration credits: we can offer a one-time migration credit applied at invoice for customers committing to a 12-month reserved package. Typical migration credit for deals in this size range is $20k–$50k (one-time). If you need a longer runway we can structure it as a monthly rebate against committed spend — happy to model both.

Next steps: Aditya will follow up with a draft commercial term sheet (platform fee option vs percent option) and a DocuSign-ready SOW. Marcus, can you confirm install packaging constraints for their air-gapped setup? Maria — I set a target to get the draft to you by EOD Tuesday (2025-08-05) so you have time for internal review.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
Attachments: Redwood_Private_Pricing_v1.xlsx, Redwood_Support_Tiers_2025.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@aurorafintech.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging questions + migration credits for VPC/on-prem

Maria — quick technical notes to complement Soojin's commercial summary:

- For air-gapped installs we provide an installer bundle plus an operator manifest. Licensing enforcement is node-based; we add a per-GPU meter for >8 GPUs. For your 6–8 GPU target the node-based package is most predictable.
- We recommend the "standard" packaging for POC (single control-plane VM + up to 8 worker GPUs). For production we suggest HA control-plane (2 vms) and an HA worker pool.
- Quantization and kernel selection: the runtime supports INT8/FP16 paths — the licensing doesn't restrict quantization, but performance optimizations for certain vendor GPUs require the premium support tier (we include tuned kernels and on-call performance tuning).
- For compliance: we can provide SOC2 Artifact export and audit logs; those are included in Enterprise support or as an add-on.

I'll prep a short install-level BOM and a recommended packaging SKU for the RFQ items and attach the BOM to the commercial draft.

— Marcus
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@aurorafintech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Aug 2025 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging questions + migration credits for VPC/on-prem

Thanks for the fast turnaround. The pricing workbook looks reasonable — procurement asked whether Redwood can:

- Confirm a one-time migration credit at $40k applied on the first invoice if we sign by 2025-08-12
- Offer a 10% discount on the fixed annual platform fee if we commit to a 24-month reserved term instead of 12 months

If you can confirm those two items, I'll put this on the expedited path and route the draft SOW through legal. We prefer DocuSign for signature — please include the SOW and the support addendum.

On the technical side, the air-gapped installer BOM will be helpful; please include checksums and a list of outbound ports (we're locked-down so specifics matter).

Looking forward to Aditya's SOW.

Best,
Maria
